research_question: What is the effect of behavioural support, compared with brief advice or no intervention (with matched pharmacotherapy background where applicable), on tobacco use cessation?
treatment_label: Behavioural support for smoking cessation (counselling/behavioural programme, delivered alone, or added to NRT, or added to varenicline)
control_label: Matched comparator without behavioural support (brief advice or no intervention; brief advice + NRT; or varenicline alone)
outcome_description: Tobacco use cessation / smoking abstinence at longest reported follow-up (e.g. continuous, prolonged, sustained or 7-day point-prevalence abstinence, biochemically validated or self-reported), extracted as number of quitters out of number randomised in each arm.
positive_direction: A positive effect (risk ratio above 1) means that participants receiving behavioural support achieved HIGHER tobacco abstinence (quit) rates than those receiving brief advice, no intervention, or the matched pharmacotherapy-only control.
search_queries: behavioural support smoking cessation randomised controlled trial abstinence
smoking cessation counselling versus brief advice trial quit rates
behavioural intervention plus nicotine replacement varenicline cessation trial outcome
inclusion_criteria: Study evaluates some form of behavioural support, counselling, or behavioural programme for tobacco/smoking cessation in people who use tobacco
Study compares the behavioural support condition against a less-intensive or no-behavioural-support comparator (brief advice, usual care, no intervention, or pharmacotherapy alone)
Study reports some quantitative cessation/abstinence outcome (quit counts, quit rates, proportions, or effect estimates) for both conditions
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between a treatment condition and a control/comparator condition (single-arm or uncontrolled pre-post designs only)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts, proportions, means+SDs, t/F statistics, or odds/risk ratios)
Completely unrelated to tobacco use cessation (e.g. focused only on alcohol or other drug use, or on smoking prevention in never-smokers)
moderators_to_extract: Intervention-combination subgroup (behavioural support alone vs + NRT vs + varenicline)
Intensity of behavioural support (number/duration of sessions)
Delivery mode (in-person individual, group, telephone, digital)
Length of follow-up for abstinence assessment
effect_size_note: Pool as risk ratios (RR) of abstinence, behavioural support vs matched control, using event counts over the number randomised (participants lost to follow-up counted as continuing smokers where reported). Keep the three intervention-combination comparisons (behavioural support alone vs brief advice/no intervention; behavioural support + NRT vs brief advice + NRT; behavioural support + varenicline vs varenicline alone) as distinct subgroups within a single pooled random-effects analysis, each matched to its own control arm. For multi-arm trials testing more than one behavioural-support variant against a single shared control group, enter each variant as its own row and divide the shared control arm's events and sample size proportionally across the variants (shared-control splitting) to avoid double-counting control participants, rather than selecting one arm or discarding variants.
